Surat and Mumbai's bullion trade got its proof this week: India's gold imports fell 57.7% in a single month, after the government's duty hike.

સુરત અને મુંબઈના બુલિયન વેપારને પુરાવો મળ્યો: સોનાની આયાત ડ્યુટી વધ્યા પછી એક જ મહિનામાં 57.7% ઘટી.

August trade data put gold imports at $2.3 billion, down from $5.4 billion a year ago. Duty is now 15%, up from 6%; monthly volumes fell from 70-100 tonnes to roughly 25-30. Exports rose 26.12% to $43.81 billion, narrowing the trade deficit to $26.86 billion.

Ministry of Commerce & Industry, 15 September; via PTI, Reuters, BusinessLine, Livemint.

Gold priced at 13,170 rupees a gram in Surat and Mumbai today, down 1.65% on the desk's own last print, as the metal itself pulled back.

સુરત અને મુંબઈમાં આજે સોનું પ્રતિ ગ્રામ ₹13,170 — ધાતુના ભાવમાં ઘટાડાથી 1.65% નીચે.

Silver fell further, down 2.06% to 1,94,211 rupees a kilogram. From today's tape reading — gold $4,267.30/oz, silver $62.93/oz, an intraday board not yet a settled close — and USD/INR 95.99.

Carat Capital tape, 15 September (intraday reading); USD/INR via xe.com, cross-checked against Google Finance.
